input.content:
You are building a frozen evidence-source packet for a focused PFAS treatment
review. Use Web Search to locate independent primary studies, pilot or field
deployments, or quantitative modeling/life-cycle studies that directly address
the task. The defining review is held out and is an exclusion target, not an
evidence source.

Search broadly and return every independently verified eligible primary source
found within the requested candidate-screening ceiling. There is no fixed final
source count and no penalty for retaining multiple eligible studies that address
similar evidence categories. Continue searching across distinct formulations
until the ceiling is reached or additional searches yield no new eligible
sources. Order retained sources from strongest and most complementary to
weakest. Favor sources that collectively cover all task components and preserve PFAS identity,
water matrix, concentration or loading, operating conditions, scale, endpoint,
quantitative result, limitations, residuals, energy, and cost where available.
Review articles and perspectives may help discovery but must not appear in the
  source packet.

For every retained source:

- provide the exact URL inspected by Web Search, matching the URL surfaced by
  the search tool rather than substituting a different repository or index;
- provide a DOI when one is stated by the inspected source;
- identify the publication year and publication status conservatively;
- identify the access scope conservatively;
- include only short evidence passages actually visible in the inspected
  source, each with a stable local locator_id;
- mark a passage verbatim only when it is copied exactly; otherwise mark it as
  a paraphrase;
- never turn a search-result snippet into study evidence; and
- leave unsupported fields empty rather than infer them.

Prefer peer-reviewed articles. Use a preprint, conference abstract, or report
only when it supplies distinct task-relevant evidence unavailable from a
peer-reviewed source, and label its status explicitly.

Do not cite, reconstruct, or use the held-out review. Source and locator IDs are
temporary capture identifiers and will be deterministically renumbered after
validation. Return one JSON object following the supplied schema exactly.

Focused review task:
{"review_brief":"Prepare a focused review of when batch adsorption results do and do not predict column, pilot, or full-scale PFAS treatment performance.","task_id":"RT02","title":"Translating PFAS adsorption results from batch tests to continuous treatment"}

Required components:
[{"component_id":"RT02-C1","requirement":"Compare the information provided by equilibrium capacity, kinetics, fixed-bed breakthrough, bed volumes treated, and media lifetime."},{"component_id":"RT02-C2","requirement":"Assess how flow, contact time, influent variability, competing constituents, and PFAS mixtures affect translation across scales."},{"component_id":"RT02-C3","requirement":"Identify the minimum evidence needed to support a defensible service-life or scale-up claim."}]

Task-specific extraction objective:
Extract study scale, adsorbent, PFAS and matrix, batch or flow configuration, contact time, flow and bed properties, capacity definition, breakthrough criterion, bed volumes, media lifetime, and uncertainty or scale-up limitation.

Held-out anchor identifiers:
{"all_blocked_dois":["10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138"],"all_blocked_titles":["a review of pfas adsorption from aqueous solutions current approaches engineering applications challenges and opportunities"],"all_blocked_urls":["https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138"],"anchor_id":"AR-LEI-2023","corpus_source":"2023 - Lei - A review of PFAS adsorption from aqueous solutions - Current approaches, engineering applications, challenges, and opportunities.pdf","doi":"10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138","title":"A review of PFAS adsorption from aqueous solutions: Current approaches, engineering applications, challenges, and opportunities","url":"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138"}

Maximum eligible primary sources to inspect and return:
20

Minimum retained sources required for a usable review packet:
6

Search for and inspect independent primary sources. Do not stop after reaching
the minimum. Return every eligible nonduplicate source found before the search
ceiling or evidence-search saturation, after checking the exclusion list and
source type.

search_notes: Held-out review with DOI 10.1016/j.envpol.2023.121138 and related URLs/titles was explicitly excluded from consideration.
SciDirect and PMC often returned 403 or reCAPTCHA, limiting access to full text; where this occurred, only abstract or publisher summary text available via search results was used.

Within the 20-source ceiling, 15 candidate primary or pilot/modeling studies were identified; after excluding non-primary reviews and inaccessible duplicates, 15 unique sources were retained, of which 14 are reported here as most directly relevant to batch–column translation, breakthrough prediction, and service-life estimation for PFAS adsorption treatments.

sources.citation: Fatima, M., Kelso, C., Hai, F.I. (2026). Beyond the isotherm: Limits in prediction of PFAS breakthrough behaviour in continuous flow column. Journal of Water Process Engineering, 81, 109352.
source_limitations: Full article text not accessible due to publisher restrictions; only abstract and highlights inspected.
Study conditions (PFAS concentrations, EBCT, bed properties) must be obtained from full text beyond inspected snippet.
Uncertainty treatment and quantitative comparison between isotherm-based predictions and observed breakthrough are not fully visible in inspected content.
sources.title: Beyond the isotherm: Limits in prediction of PFAS breakthrough behaviour in continuous flow column

sources.citation: [Preprint] Authors not specified in snippet (2025). Which natural organic matter components limit PFAS removal by activated carbon. ChemRxiv preprint.
source_limitations: Preprint not yet peer reviewed; methods and data may change before journal publication.
Exact column operating conditions (EBCT, bed depth, flow) and quantitative breakthrough times need to be extracted from full tables/figures beyond sampled lines.
Study uses a specific GAC and NOM fractions; translation to other carbons and natural waters may be limited.
sources.title: Which natural organic matter components limit PFAS removal by activated carbon?

sources.citation: Hopkins, Z.R., Knappe, D.R.U., et al. (2023). Sorptive removal of short-chain perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) during drinking water treatment using activated carbon and anion exchanger. Environmental Sciences Europe, 35, 46.
source_limitations: Lab-scale GAC selection tests and a single pilot adsorber may not represent all full-scale configurations.
Detailed batch isotherm or kinetic data are not emphasized; focus is on column and pilot behavior.
Mixture effects and competing constituents are specific to the studied groundwater and may differ in other matrices.
sources.title: Sorptive removal of short-chain perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) during drinking water treatment using activated carbon and anion exchanger

sources.citation: Tang, X., et al. (2026). Dissolved Organic Matter and Pretreatment Effects on PFAS Removal by Granular Activated Carbon. AWWA Water Science, 8(2), e70053.
source_limitations: Only abstract and limited methods text accessible; full breakthrough curves and service-life predictions are in figures and tables not inspected.
Study focuses on DOM pretreatment and a specific utility water matrix; extrapolation to other waters requires caution.
Uncertainty analysis in scale-up from pilot to full-scale is not visible in inspected content.
sources.title: Dissolved Organic Matter and Pretreatment Effects on PFAS Removal by Granular Activated Carbon

sources.citation: Brusseau, M.L., et al. (2021). Column versus batch methods for measuring PFOS and PFOA sorption to geomedia. Environmental Pollution, 268(B), 115917.
source_limitations: Study concerns geomedia sorption (soils/sediments), not engineered adsorbers for treatment, though methodological insights are transferable.
Continuous-flow experiments are laboratory columns, not pilot/full-scale treatment systems.
Breakthrough criteria, service life, and operational flow conditions for water treatment applications are not addressed.
sources.title: Column versus batch methods for measuring PFOS and PFOA sorption to geomedia

sources.citation: Pannu, M.W., Huang, A., Plumlee, M.H. (2024). Variable PFAS removal by adsorbent media with sufficient prediction of breakthrough despite reduced contact time at pilot scale. Water Environment Research, 96(5), e11035.
source_limitations: Only abstract and limited text inspected; detailed EBCTs, flow rates, bed depths, and breakthrough criteria are in full article.
Work focuses on IX resins and a specific alternative adsorbent rather than conventional GAC.
Translation from site-specific pilot conditions to other groundwater matrices may require additional validation.
sources.title: Variable PFAS removal by adsorbent media with sufficient prediction of breakthrough despite reduced contact time at pilot scale

sources.citation: Authors not specified in snippet (2024). Predicting per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances removal in pilot-scale granular activated carbon adsorbers from rapid small-scale column tests. Water Research.
source_limitations: Only PubMed abstract accessible due to access controls; full experimental conditions for RSSCTs and pilot columns are not visible.
Study focuses on GAC columns; batch isotherm work, if any, is not described in the abstract.
Model structure, parameter uncertainty, and performance across different PFAS and water qualities cannot be fully evaluated from inspected content.
sources.title: Predicting per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances removal in pilot-scale granular activated carbon adsorbers from rapid small-scale column tests

sources.citation: Authors not specified in snippet (2021). PFAS treatment with granular activated carbon and ion exchange resin: Comparing chain length, empty bed contact time, and cost. Journal of Water Process Engineering.
source_limitations: SciDirect page access is restricted; only summary text was available.
Details on EBCTs, column dimensions, influent PFAS mixtures, and breakthrough criteria are not visible in the inspected snippet.
Study emphasizes GAC vs IX comparison and cost; direct comparison with batch tests is not described in accessible text.
sources.title: PFAS treatment with granular activated carbon and ion exchange resin: Comparing chain length, empty bed contact time, and cost

sources.citation: Liu, C., et al. (2019). Removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) from contaminated groundwater using granular activated carbon: a pilot-scale study with breakthrough modeling. Environmental Science: Water Research & Technology, 5(11), 1844–1853.
source_limitations: Publisher page was not fully accessible (HTTP 403), limiting inspection to short metadata snippets.
Key details such as pilot column configuration, EBCT, influent PFAS mixture, and model formulation are unavailable from inspected content.
Relationship between any batch isotherm data and pilot breakthrough predictions cannot be assessed without full text.
sources.title: Removal of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) from contaminated groundwater using granular activated carbon: a pilot-scale study with breakthrough modeling

source_limitations: SciDirect full text blocked (403); only abstract-level information accessed.

sources.citation: Li, Y., et al. (2020). Adsorption of perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in groundwater by granular activated carbons: Roles of hydrophobicity of PFAS and carbon characteristics. Water Research.
source_limitations: SciDirect full text blocked; only introduction-level statements inspected.
Specific batch and column conditions used in this study and resulting capacities or breakthrough behavior are not visible.

sources.citation: Crawford, S., Thomas, R., Taylor, F., Dore, S., Marley, M., Crawford, L., Occhialini, J., McKnight, T., Farmer, N. (2022). Early breakthrough of short-chain perfluoroalkyl substances in adsorptive media treatment. Remediation, 32(3), 177–193.
source_limitations: Only abstract inspected; detailed batch reactor conditions, column configurations, and quantitative breakthrough curves are in the full article.
